architecture_decisions: Preserve the model router’s existing bounded attempt records and failure classification.
validations: In candidate recovery, inspect only that bounded diagnostic.
AC-01: validate protected requirement — `ImplementationGenerationFailure` exposes bounded router failure classification without raw provider/model output.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — A parsed proposal rejected by the protected proposal validator causes the next admitted candidate for the same work unit to receive static server-owned safe-patch repair guidance.
AC-03: validate protected requirement — Provider/rate-limit failures do not receive validator-specific repair guidance and remain governed by existing candidate/provider recovery semantics.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — Repair guidance states the exact safe-patch requirements needed by the unchanged server validator, including exact path/digest binding and strict single-file unified-diff form.
AC-05: validate protected requirement — The existing `max_reassignments_per_work_unit` bound and eligible-agent set remain authoritative. No additional unbounded retry loop is introduced.
AC-06: validate protected requirement — Repair guidance grants no canonical source, lineage, Git, deployment, REVIEW, Engineering Run transition, credential, or network authority.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — If all admitted candidates still fail, exhaustion evidence records only bounded server-owned rejection kind values and preserves `worker_process_loss=false` with all mutation claims false.
AC-08: validate protected requirement — A first candidate that passes the protected proposal validator follows the existing path with no repair guidance or semantic change.
AC-09: validate protected requirement — Tests prove validation classification, validation-guided next-candidate repair, provider-failure separation, finite recovery, and bounded diagnostics.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — Protected spec/plan validation, focused tests, full API regression, Bounded Autonomy, client/browser, protected promotion, and DSPy release gates are green before merge.
risks: Provider exhaustion/rate-limit failures continue without validator-specific guidance.

critique:
:
- `SafeImplementationEngine` and `TextPatchEngine` remain authoritative and unchanged.
- A rejected candidate remains non-authoritative and non-mutating.
- Only router-classified `VALIDATION_EXHAUSTED` failures may trigger safe-patch repair guidance.
- Repair guidance is server-owned static text.
- Repair guidance may be appended only to a later already-admitted candidate generation request for the same work unit.
- Candidate count and alternate-agent budget remain unchanged; this release does not add an unbounded or hidden same-model loop.
- Exact acceptance ownership, candidate admission, disposable validation, independent evaluation, routing, canonical mutation, Git delivery, Preview delivery, REVIEW, and production authority remain unchanged.
